items.headline: The Ultimate Guide to Prompt Engineering in 2026
items.summary: Enterprise AI prompt engineering in 2026 focuses on treating prompts as reusable assets with version control, testing, and governance. The number one best practice is writing success criteria and an output contract upfront, as structured prompts beat length. Key techniques include clear role definition, few-shot examples, explicit constraints, and comparative testing across evaluation criteria like accuracy, completeness, tone, and compliance.

items.headline: Klarna's AI Replaces 700 Agents, Saves $40M/Year — The Full Story
items.summary: Klarna's AI customer service assistant (launched February 2024, built with OpenAI) automated 67% of customer conversations, reduced resolution time from 11 minutes to under 2 minutes, cut repeat inquiries by 25%, and saved $40M annually by avoiding 700 new hires. However, the 2026 retrospective documents a costly partial reversal in 2025 due to quality degradation on complex cases and institutional knowledge loss. The lesson is AI scales tier-one volume, humans move up the value chain, not wholesale replacement.

items.headline: Deloitte's AI fiasco: Why chatbots hallucinate and who else got caught
items.summary: The Australian government hired Deloitte to review a welfare compliance system. The 237-page report contained fabricated references to sources and experts that do not exist. Deloitte admitted it used Azure OpenAI GPT-4o without disclosure and refunded part of the AU$439,000 fee. This marked one of the first public cases of government repayment over undisclosed AI use. In May 2026, a similar EY Canada report on loyalty programs was withdrawn after most citations were found to be hallucinated, including fake McKinsey reports.

items.headline: U.S. Companies Face EU AI Act's Possible August 2026 Compliance Deadline
items.summary: August 2, 2026 marks the critical compliance deadline for Annex III high-risk AI systems under the EU AI Act, including AI used in employment, credit decisions, education, and law enforcement. The regulation has extraterritorial scope affecting U.S. tech and SaaS companies serving EU customers. Non-compliance fines reach up to 35 million euros or a percentage of global annual turnover. Compliance requires integrating AI risk into GRC frameworks, establishing cross-functional governance structures, and assembling technical audit files.
